A first stop before [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the DX7 is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **DX7** was made by **Yamaha** and came out in **1983** (Wikipedia, "Yamaha DX7").
- "The DX7 was the first commercially successful digital synthesizer" (Wikipedia).
- It has **16 voices** and **32 memories** (DX7 manual, introduction).

## Its sound

- It uses **FM**: one sine wave (a *modulator*) wobbles the pitch of another (a *carrier*) very fast, which makes new harmonics (DX7 manual, p. 23).
- It has **six operators** joined in one of **32 algorithms** (manual, p. 24).
- There is **no filter**: the sound changes when a modulator's **output level** changes (manual, pp. 34-35).
- Each operator has its own envelope of 4 rates and 4 levels (manual, p. 26).

## Guided tour

Each step loads a worked example and changes one thing. Learn more about FM in [Sound 8: FM](sound-fm.qmd).

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="dx7-saw" data-set="{&quot;o2l&quot;:0}"><p><b>A sine wave.</b> Operator 1 alone (operator 2's level at 0). Listen: pure and plain.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="dx7-saw" data-set="{&quot;o2l&quot;:70}"><p><b>Add a little FM.</b> Operator 2's <b>output level</b> to 70. Listen: brighter, buzzier.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="dx7-saw"><p><b>More FM.</b> Operator 2 at 99, the manual's first exercise (pp. 34-35). Listen: like a sawtooth, with no filter at all.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="dx7-bell"><p><b>A bell.</b> The modulator at 3.5 times the carrier's frequency. Listen: a bell, because the harmonics are not in a row.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="dx7-ep"><p><b>An electric-piano-like tine.</b> Two stacks of operators. Listen for the "ding" at the start of each note.</p></div>
```

## Famous records

Named in Wikipedia, "Yamaha DX7":

- Prince, "When Doves Cry"
- a-ha, "Take On Me" (the "Bass 1" preset)
- Berlin, "Take My Breath Away" (the "Bass 2" preset)
- Brian Eno, *Apollo: Atmospheres and Soundtracks*

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>In FM, the operator that changes another&#x27;s pitch is called…</b></p><ul><li>The modulator</li><li>The filter</li><li>The mixer</li><li>The drum</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 23.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>How does the DX7 make a sound brighter without a filter?</b></p><ul><li>Turn a modulator's output level up</li><li>Turn the reverb up</li><li>Play faster</li><li>It cannot</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Steps 1-3.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="2"><p><b>How many operators does it have?</b></p><ul><li>Two</li><li>Four</li><li>Six</li><li>Thirty-two</li></ul><p class="ik-why">32 is the number of algorithms.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What was the DX7 the first of?</b></p><ul><li>Commercially successful digital synths</li><li>Electric guitars</li><li>Drum machines</li><li>Radios</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
```
